properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js 1.1.3 and 1.1.7 (declared at yarn.lock:11748 and 11756) implement the SHA-2 family (and SHA-1) in pure JS. In this scaffold-eth monorepo they arrive transitively: elliptic depends on hash.js for ECDSA message hashing (yarn.lock:8705), and the ethers/web3 toolchain uses it via @ethersproject/sha2. Dependency inventory entry: ships in the build whether or not the app calls it directly; the canonical weakest member (SHA-1) is quantum-safe for preimage but collision-deprecated.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic 6.5.2 and 6.5.4 (yarn.lock:8701, 8714) provide ECDSA + ECDH over secp256k1 (and other curves) in pure JS. In this repo it is the account-signature primitive of the Ethereum stack: react-app depends on ethers ^5.4.1 whose @ethersproject/signing-key uses elliptic for secp256k1 ECDSA signing of every transaction/message. Quantum-unsafe signature, deadline risk (ML-DSA-65), not harvest-now. Changeable only upstream (replaceable by wallet SDKs moving to PQ signatures).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2@^3.0.17 resolved 3.1.2 (yarn.lock:16653) is the browserify PBKDF2 shim built over sha.js hashes, pulled in via crypto-browserify in the web3/ipfs dependency chain of the react-app. PBKDF2 itself is a KDF (parameterised by hash+iterations); the lockfile cannot show iteration counts, which live in callers. Keystore (V3) wallet files in the ethers stack derive keys via PBKDF2/scrypt at 262144 iterations.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 as provided by @noble/hashes 1.1.2/1.1.3 (yarn.lock:3099, 3104), pulled transitively via ethereum-cryptography in the @walletconnect/web3/@arbitrum stack of the react-app. Hash use (commitments, digests) is not harvest-now-decrypt-later urgent; SHA-256 is Grover-square-rooted only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 as provided by @noble/hashes 1.1.2/1.1.3 (yarn.lock:3099, 3104) in the react-app's wallet-connectivity dependency chain. Available in the shipped library; no direct call site in the app source I read.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3 as provided by @noble/hashes 1.1.2/1.1.3 (yarn.lock:3099, 3104). Note the Ethereum ecosystem's dominant hash is keccak256 (pre-standardisation SHA-3 padding), which lives in js-sha3/keccak packages; this entry is the FIPS-202 SHA-3 exported by @noble/hashes in the wallet-connectivity chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js 2.0.4 and 3.0.1 (yarn.lock:19508, 19513) implement the scrypt KDF. In the Ethereum stack scrypt is what encrypts keystore (V3) wallet JSON files — @ethersproject/json-wallets uses it at N=131072 default — so this repo's wallet import/export path depends on it. Memory-hard KDF, quantum-safe as a KDF; the parameter set (N,r,p) lives in callers, not the lockfile.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js (yarn.lock:19737, resolves sha.js 2.4.x) provides streamable SHA-1/SHA-224/SHA-256/SHA-384/SHA-512. It is the hash engine underneath the pbkdf2 browserify shim (pbkdf2 depends on sha.js), so it ships in the react-app bundle via crypto-browserify. The SHA-1 member it exports is collision-broken — worth noting if any caller selects it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic 6.5.2/6.5.4 (yarn.lock:8701, 8714): pure-JS secp256k1 ECDSA/ECDH/EdDSA provider. This is the library behind Ethereum account keys in this repo's ethers-based toolchain, and also feeds crypto-browserify's create-ecdh. Ships in the react-app bundle via wallet providers; presence is the inventory fact, call sites are in the wallet SDKs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes 1.1.2 and 1.1.3 (yarn.lock:3099, 3104) is a modern hash library (SHA-256/384/512, SHA-3/keccak, BLAKE family, ripemd160) pulled via ethereum-cryptography in the wallet-connectivity chain of react-app. Changeable here only by bumping upstream wallet SDKs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: selfsigned 1.10.11 (yarn.lock:19565) generates self-signed X.509 certificates using node-forge ^0.10.0. It arrives via webpack-dev-server inside react-scripts 4, used to mint the throwaway cert for the local HTTPS dev server — dev tooling only, not shipped to users, and its RSA-based certs are disposable. Changeable here (upgrade react-scripts or drop HTTPS dev). Related X.509 objects ALG-0e533e47/ALG-1847d707 cover the cert output.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js 1.1.3 and 1.1.7 (yarn.lock:11748, 11756): pure-JS hash library (SHA-1/2, ripemd160). Direct dependency of elliptic (yarn.lock:8705) — i.e., part of the secp256k1 ECDSA signing path — and of the ethers sha2 module. Available in the shipped library; the app itself does not import it directly.
